correctness.rationale: The jump-to-slope matrix H=B(I+lambda D2^T D2)^(-1)U is nonnegative exactly when every monotone input is sent to a monotone output. Exact rational-function factorizations give the cutoffs 1/6, 7/10 and (14+sqrt(181))/15. The four-point sharp decrease follows from the unique negative corner entry and the derivative 1-12lambda-92lambda^2. A perturbation at lambda=0 proves failure for small positive strength at every length >=4; affine-projector convergence gives eventual positivity for each fixed length. Fourier coefficients of h(theta)=[1+lambda(2-2cos theta)^2]^-1 have zero second moment, nontrivial spectrum and exponential decay, forcing a negative coefficient. Boundary-residual convergence of finite resolvents transfers the associated decreasing step output to sufficiently long finite samples for each fixed lambda>0. Rational inversion tests and optional finite numerical checks passed (VERIFY_OK).

value.rationale: For unconstrained trend smoothing, keeping the ordering of observed monotone data is a substantive shape-stability property independent of range preservation. The complete first nontrivial parameter classifications, attained sharp adjacent-drop bound, and rigorous no-uniform-strength obstruction provide natural safety boundaries for fixed-length and varying-length data rather than an unmotivated isolated numerical constant.
